Team / Julian — thanks, I reviewed the redlines and the Subprocessor List. Below is recommended text and rationale. Happy to refine.

Recommended clause (candidate):
"Redwood will provide Customer with prior written notice of the addition of any new subprocessor that will have access to Customer Personal Data at least 21 calendar days prior to such subprocessor commencing processing. Customer will have 14 calendar days from receipt of such notice to raise a written objection on reasonable grounds (e.g., inability to comply with technical or organizational measures). If Customer and Redwood cannot resolve the objection within an additional 7 calendar days, the parties shall escalate to senior legal representatives to seek a resolution. If no resolution is reached, the Customer's sole remedy shall be to suspend use of the affected Service with respect to the impacted data processing activities or terminate the agreement for convenience with a 30-day wind-down period."

Rationale: 21/14 balances operational deployment needs and gives customers meaningful review time. The extra 7-day escalation window avoids immediate service disruption while creating an explicit escalation path. We should also include a sentence binding subprocessors to equivalent contractual terms and confirming that any subprocessor processing EU data will be subject to appropriate transfer safeguards (SCCs or equivalent).

Regarding Acme's ask for 30/30: it's negotiable but materially increases cloud vendor coordination time; for operational scalability we prefer the 21/14/7 stack. If Acme insists on 30/30, we should ask for an explicit provisioning SLA exception and commit to a longer sign-off timeline in DocuSign.

DocuSign note: once language is agreed, legal will prepare the final DPA and we can seed the envelope. Recommend we avoid multiple concurrent envelopes to reduce versioning risk.
